 Preview: Utah Jazz Return Home to Host Phoenix Suns in NBA Cup Action
 Eric Spyropoulos ● @EricSpyroNBA Digital Writer November 19, 2026 4:05 PM MST The Utah Jazz have returned home with some momentum. 
 A shorthanded Utah squad went to Los Angeles for a back-to-back set of games earlier this week against the Clippers and Lakers, ultimately leaving with a sweep that was built on impressive defense and elite execution in fourth quarters. 
 Utah’s most recent win was a 109-97 affair against the Lakers, who owned the league’s top-ranked offense going into Wednesday’s contest. However, led by Josh Green and Josh Okogie, the Jazz made life difficult for Luka Dončić throughout the night (10-of-28 shooting with nine turnovers) and held Los Angeles to just 97 points. The Lakers only shot 38-percent from the field and turned it over 18 times, which helped Utah’s offense. 
 Meanwhile, on the other end of the floor, Keyonte George delivered a second consecutive 30-point double-double, effectively balancing his scoring and playmaking to drive Utah’s third win of the season.
 The Jazz now return home to the Delta Center for an NBA Cup matchup against the Phoenix Suns.
 Phoenix (7-7) has righted the ship, having gone 6-2 after a disappointing 1-5 start to the new season. The Suns are certainly relying on offense to win games, ranking ninth in offensive rating and just 25th in defensive rating as of Thursday morning. One again, Devin Booker continues to lead the way for Phoenix, as the five-time All-Star is averaging 24.8 points and 5.4 assists per game.
 The Suns won two of the three meetings between the two teams last season.
 Jazz injury report: 
 OUT - Jonas Aidoo (G League - Two-Way), Kobe Bufkin (G League - Two-Way), Harrison Ingram (G League - Two-Way), Jaren Jackson (Right Knee; MCL Tear), Lauri Markkanen (Right Hand; Fracture), Jusuf Nurkić (Right Foot; 2nd Plantar Plate Tear)
 Suns injury report: 
 OUT - Mark Williams (Left Shoulder; Surgery) 
 Here are three keys to Friday’s game.
 Limiting turnovers  
 Phoenix will provide a difficult matchup for Utah in one important area Friday night and that is related to ball security.
 The Suns rarely turn the ball over themselves on the offensive end (13.7 percent of possessions, fifth-lowest in the league), but it’s their activity on the defensive end that the Jazz must focus on. Phoenix has struggled in nearly every area of defense outside of forcing turnovers, as it ranks fourth in opponent turnover percentage.
 If the Jazz can limit their mistakes (they coughed it up 23 times against the Lakers and rank 25th in turnover percentage on the year), they should be able to carve out consistent offense against a struggling Suns defense. 
 The battle on the boards  
 While Phoenix has thrived in the turnover department, the other area of the possession game has caused issues for Jordan Ott’s squad. 
 The Suns rank 20th in offensive rebound percentage and dead-last in defensive rebound percentage, which can create opportunities for the Jazz to capitalize on. Utah hasn’t relied on offensive rebounding this season as the team navigates a shorthanded frontcourt rotation, but Friday’s game should be an opportunity to crash the boards aggressively. 
 Elite defensive rebounding has been a calling card for the Jazz early in the season (ninth in defensive rebound percentage), which will need to be present Friday night to ensure that the Suns don’t generate additional scoring opportunities.
 Attacking from beyond the arc  
 As mentioned earlier, the Suns have struggled on the defensive end when they haven’t been able to force turnovers. 
 Phoenix ranks 22nd in opponent effective field-goal percentage, 30th in opponent offensive rebound percentage, and 23rd in opponent free-throw rate. A specific area that teams have been able to exploit is Phoenix’s perimeter defense. 
 Over 40 percent of opponent shot attempts against the Suns have come from three this season, with teams converting on 38.3 percent of those looks, the fourth-highest percentage in the league. Although the Jazz have struggled at times to knock down shots, the tide is turning for Will Hardy’s squad as of late. 
 In the last four games, Utah shot 42.3 percent from downtown on 39 attempts per contest. That efficiency leads the league during this small stretch of play, and if the Jazz can keep generating quality looks, they will have opportunities to stretch the Suns defense out Friday night. 
 Friday’s game tips off at 7:30 p.m. MT. Tune in to the pregame show with Alema Harrington and Mike Smith beginning at 7 p.m. MT on Jazz+!
